9mothers-9-mothers:ashbyhq:d25a11b2-200d.description: Location: Onsite — Austin, TX Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full-Time Job Title: Manufacturing Engineering Lead About 9 Mothers The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield. Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack. Why 9 Mothers? While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground. Position Summary We are hiring a Manufacturing Engineering Lead as our first hire focused on manufacturing rather than R&D. Our robotic turret product is moving from engineering-built units toward repeatable production, and we need someone to plant the seeds of our manufacturing process with a clear eye on how that process will scale. This is a ground-floor role. Today there is no manufacturing organization; you will define its foundations. That starts with the manufacturing strategy itself: what we build in-house in Austin, what we place with contract manufacturers and suppliers, and how that split evolves as volume grows. The processes, documentation, quality practices, and supplier relationships you establish in year one are what the production org will be built on, and for the right person there is real potential to grow into leading that organization as it takes shape. This is also a hands-on role in the most literal sense. The first manufacturing instructions will be written by you, from builds you perform yourself, bolt by bolt. We are looking for someone who has done this before: someone who has taken hardware from prototype into production at least once and can describe concretely what that transition looked like, the role they personally played in it, and what they would do differently this time. Essential Duties - Define the manufacturing strategy. Own the make/buy analysis for the product. Decide what we build and assemble in-house versus what we source from suppliers and contract manufacturers and build the roadmap for how those split changes with volume. - Build early units yourself and write the first MIs. Turn the bolts with your own hands-on early builds, and capture what you learn as the manufacturing instructions, travelers, fixtures, and process documentation the production line will inherit. - Stand up the production process. Establish routings, assembly and test stations, tooling and fixtures, and the flow of material through the building. Start lean, but structure it so it scales instead of being thrown away at 10x volume. - Drive design for manufacturability. Partner with mechanical, electrical, and firmware engineering while designs are still fluid. Push DFM/DFA, tolerance and process-capability thinking, and part-count reduction into the product before it hardens. - Qualify and manage suppliers. Select machine shops, fabricators, and contract manufacturers. Own first-article inspection, supplier corrective action, and the working relationships that keep parts arriving on spec and on time. - Lay the quality foundation. Build right-sized quality practices from scratch: incoming inspection, in-process checks, end-of-line test, nonconformance and corrective action, and unit-level serialization and traceability appropriate to NFA-regulated manufacturing. - Own build data and BOM discipline. Keep manufacturing BOMs, revisions, and as-built records clean and trustworthy. Stand up or shape the MRP/ERP tooling we grow into, working with engineering’s P

brinc-brinc:ashbyhq:d4beac4b-fafd-49bc-9.description: ABOUT BRINC: At BRINC, we are redefining public safety with an innovative ecosystem of life-saving tools. Our journey started with the development of drones and ruggedized throw phones, designed to access unsafe areas and establish communication to de-escalate situations. Today, we've expanded into creating and deploying 911 response networks, where drones are dispatched to 911 calls to provide real-time visual data, enhancing safety and enabling de-escalation-focused responses. Our cutting-edge solutions are utilized by over 600 public safety agencies across America and the company has raised over $150M from investors, including Index Ventures, Motorola Solutions, Sam Altman, Dylan Field, Mike Volpe, Alexandr Wang and more. At BRINC, we are committed to recruiting the world's best talent to join us in our mission to support first responders in saving lives. ABOUT THIS ROLE: We are seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer to embed onsite with BRINC’s most critical customers and own their success in the field. You will support the installation and commissioning of BRINC’s end-to-end drone systems and live operational flights, triage and debug issues across hardware, firmware, and software, and implement fixes on-site. You will be the direct line between the customer and engineering at headquarters, turning what you see in real operations into shipped features and resolved issues. This is a hybrid of software engineering, technical support, and product expertise, and it suits someone equally comfortable writing code, flying a drone, and briefing customer command staff. This role is upwards of 90% travel and suits someone genuinely excited to be on the road and embedded with our customers. Expect multi-week deployments at key customer sites, with regular travel to BRINC’s Seattle headquarters in between. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: - Deploy onsite for multi-week engagements with critical customers to install, configure, and commission BRINC drones, robotic drone nests, remote controllers, and proprietary LiveOps software into live 911 response operations. - Support live operational flights, including preparation testing, pre-operational briefings with contingencies, and debriefs with customer personnel and BRINC teams. - Triage and debug issues in the field across software, firmware, hardware, networking, and RF, driving them to root cause under operational time pressure. - Implement and validate fixes on-site. Write, test, and deploy code and configuration changes, then upstream that work into the mainline product. - Serve as the primary technical liaison between the customer and engineering at headquarters, translating field observations into reproducible bug reports, requirements, and feature specifications. - Rotate back to BRINC’s Seattle headquarters to work directly with embedded, perception, controls, test, and manufacturing engineers, landing new features and fixes and validating them in the operational environment before broad release. - Maintain deep technical expertise in BRINC products and proprietary software, a high level of flying proficiency, and an FAA Part 107 Pilot’s License with all required recurrent training. - Build trust-based relationships with customers and public safety agencies, and remain a calm, credible presence during mission-critical incidents. - Document issues, create knowledge base articles, and contribute to training materials and runbooks so field learnings scale to the team and to the customer. - Participate in an after-hours support rotation to ensure continuous service for agencies operating 24/7/365. - Responsibly manage assigned BRINC equipment and maintain its functionality and appearance in front of our public safety partners. QUALIFICATIONS: - 4+ years of industry experience in software engineering, field engineering, systems engineering, or technical support of complex hardware systems. - Proven experience troubleshooting complex technical systems across hardware, firmware, and software. - Abi
